## Spec-compliance review: US-01-02, PR #4, second retry round (fix range 06b43b6..dbfde5b)

**Verdict: COMPLIANT.** Nothing blocking. I found 10 non-blocking points.

I checked all 50 questions in both languages against the four Q29 checks, MOD-01-F04/F06/F07/F14 and DEC-47 option c:
- **Options:** none of the 50 questions offers options in either language. There is no either/or, "czy", "or", "albo" or "lub" anywhere in the deck.
- **Second correct answers:** I found no genuinely correct second answer that the near-miss cells missed.
- **Polish/English meaning:** no real mismatches. "łap"/"legs" (3p-03), "boisko"/"playing field" (3p-43) and "z wiejskiego podwórka"/"farm animal" (3p-37) mean the same thing.
- **Answer grammar:** the Polish answers agree grammatically with their questions, e.g. "Białego.", "Oczami.", "Na zielonym."
- **Content kinds:** 13 educational, 12 popular-science, 13 nature, 12 trivia, so each is at least 5.

### DEC-47 and the decision log
- DEC-47 in `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/docs/specs/DECISIONS.md` says "Option c" and is decided by the product owner. Its content matches the ruling: open questions only, no options in the text, near misses recorded and justified per row, 4+/5+ under the same rule, DEC-46 format unchanged. The `Affects` field now also lists MOD-03-U02, DSC-04-04, SRC-01-17 and SRC-01-18.
- The owner's actual question and answer are not stored in the repo, so I matched DEC-47 against your brief.
- **Append-only against main holds:** `git diff origin/main...dbfde5b -- docs/specs/DECISIONS.md` has no removed lines, only DEC-46 and DEC-47 added. DEC-47 was reworded inside the PR (commits d3a77eb, 9c9996d, c2800ad), but it never reached main, so no confirmed entry was edited.

### Evidence
- **CI on dbfde5b:** run 38603546684 ("Acceptance tests (Android 12 emulator)") finished with success. Artifact `og-test-results`:
  - unit tests: 53, 0 failures, 0 skipped
  - release-apk: 7, 0 failures
  - Maestro: 3+1 flows, 0 failures
- **Every required test is green:**
  - AC-01-02-1 (4 tests)
  - AC-01-02-2 (4)
  - AC-01-02-3 (5)
  - AC-01-02-4 (5, including the new step 4 near-miss check and step 5 no-options check)
  - AC-01-02-5 (16)
  - AC-01-02-6 (3)
  - AC-01-02-7 (unit step plus release-bundle step 2)
  - TC-01-02 is absent from the artifact. That is correct: DEC-44 and DEC-46 defer it to US-03-01.
- **Locally:** `npx jest tests/unit` gives 8 suites and 40 tests, all passing.
- **PR body:** its "Age-suitability record" section is byte-identical to `/Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/docs/delivery/content-checks/US-01-02-3-plus.md`, which I confirmed with a diff.
- **Scope:** the fix range touches only the deck, the record, the AC-01-02-4 test and doc, and DECISIONS. No out-of-scope or constitution issues.

### Acceptance criteria
| # | Verdict | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | met | AC-01-02-1, green in CI |
| 2 | met | AC-01-02-2, green |
| 3 | met | AC-01-02-3, green (13/12/13/12) |
| 4 | met | record in the PR body plus AC-01-02-4 steps 1–5, green |
| 5 | met | AC-01-02-5, 16 breakage tests, green |
| 6 | met | AC-01-02-6, green |
| 7 | met | AC-01-02-7 unit test and release-bundle step, green; TC-01-02 deferred by DEC-44/46 |

### Non-blocking findings
- **N1:** 3p-17 (deck line 198, record line 34) says the moon "is sometimes round and sometimes thin" ("raz jest okrągłe, a raz cienkie"). The record claims "the question now says how it looks", but it still says "is". The verifiable check is generous here.
- **N2:** several near-miss cells don't do what DEC-47 asks ("why each is ruled out"):
  - 3p-03, 3p-25, 3p-28, 3p-39, 3p-48 and 3p-50 (lines 20, 42, 45, 56, 65, 67) list the question the slot used to hold, which is history, not a near miss.
  - 3p-05 "a spoon" and 3p-21 "a rainbow" (lines 22, 38) give no reason.
  - 3p-04 (line 21) has only one near miss.
- **N3:** the test's `OFFERS_OPTIONS` (test file line 25) only catches "czy" in Polish and "or" in English. A Polish "albo"/"lub" either/or slips through whenever the English text avoids "or".
- **N4:** 3p-28 (deck line 330) doesn't list the hermit crab (krab pustelnik) as a near miss. A 3-year-old is unlikely to say it.
- **N5:** 3p-08 (deck line 90): a parent could say "the brain" sees, which is pedantic. It isn't in the cell.
- **N6:** 3p-25 (deck line 294), filling a watering can, is labelled `popular-science` but is everyday or nature content. Relabelling it would still leave 11 popular-science questions, above the minimum of 5.
- **N7:** 3p-20 (deck line 234): "pora roku"/"season" is an abstract word for a 3-year-old, so the "known words" pass is generous.
- **N8:** the 3p-43 record row (line 60) says a balloon "does not bounce", which is weak reasoning.
- **N9:** 3p-23 (deck line 270): the English "falls … and we go sledging on it" is clumsy.
- **N10:** the loop's run report `test-runs/2026-10-14_190107/run.json` lists every AC-01-02-* as skipped, even though its junit files show them passing. The earlier runs 160342 and 182139 have the same mismatch, so it is tooling outside this diff. The PR body still cites this run as "pass", and its impact block still reads "not run on this head" with 8-cell row wording.
